topic: McDonald's first CFO built the company on real estate, not burgers (Franchise Realty Corporation)
title: McDonald's Is Secretly a Real Estate Company
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_script: You think McDonald's sells burgers? Think again. McDonald's is secretly a real estate empire. The real money is in the land. Meet Harry J. Sonneborn. He was McDonald's first CFO. Sonneborn saw the true opportunity. It wasn't just about selling food. His plan was simple. But brilliant. McDonald's would buy prime land. Then, it would lease that land to its franchisees. He created the Franchise Realty Corporation. This corporation owned the land. Franchisees paid rent to McDonald's. This rent was a percentage of sales. It also included a fixed base amount. This setup gave McDonald's control. It provided a stable, growing income stream. Much more reliable than burger profits. McDonald's became a landlord first. A burger joint second. This real estate model funded massive expansion. It built the global brand you know. The next time you eat a Big Mac, remember the land beneath your feet. That's the real Sneaky Deal.
